date: 2026-11-20 (0.12.10, one run per model and arm) and 2026-11-21 (0.12.11, three runs per arm with qwen3-coder:30b)
hardware: One Apple Silicon Mac, 128 GB unified memory, macOS; router, herd-node and Ollama on the same machine
herd: 0.12.10, then 0.12.11, from Homebrew (router and herd-node), default settings, telemetry off; each run names its version
method: docs/experiments/idle-keep-alive.py: unload the model, send one request (cold), send another (warm), wait idle_s with no traffic, check /api/ps, send a third. The arms alternate (direct, herd, direct, herd), one at a time on the same Ollama; each run records its repetition and its start time (started_at, UTC). The 0.12.10 runs are one per model and arm (repetition 1), from before start times were recorded; the 0.12.11 runs are three per arm with qwen3-coder:30b, alternating direct and herd. Requests: 'Reply with the word ready.', 8-token cap, temperature 0, streaming; TTFT is the first streamed line.
finding: Ollama unloads a model after 5 idle minutes, so the next direct request reloads it. Herd sends keep_alive -1 on the requests it routes, so through Herd the model was still loaded after the same idle time. The memory stays held until something evicts the model. Replicated on 0.12.11: after 6 idle minutes the next direct request took 2.87 to 2.88 s (the model had unloaded) and through Herd 0.38 s (still loaded), in all three runs.

warm_pairs_llama3_2_1b.note: Same machine, loopback; checks that the first warm samples (58 ms) were start-up noise
